A token that starts with a double quote runs to the closing double quote, and a backslash inside it escapes the next character. bin/slice also accepts a bare 'X,Y' and spaces around the comma.

'slice run' and 'slice bench' give each child test a new value that holds only '--instance <i>,<n>' (bin/slice:3464, bin/slice:4701, bin/slice:1908). The other tokens of the inherited value do not reach the tests, and a CTest ENVIRONMENT entry with this name is overridden. bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py also replaces the whole inherited value. notes: Verification of the first agent's inventory of 98 entries. Result: 101 entries. Added 3 (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY). Removed 0. Corrected 24. Duty A: the helper baseline_only.py printed '0 scan names in area python-bin are absent from the sweep inventory', so there was no absent scan name to resolve. Duty B, methods: (1) a new syntax-tree pass over all 63 files for os.environ subscripts, get, pop, setdefault, 'in', os.getenv, monkeypatch.setenv and delenv, every dictionary literal with an upper-case key and every upper-case keyword argument; (2) a token pass that listed every upper-case word inside string literals and comments that is not in the first agent's list (274 words, each one judged); (3) a pass over all string literals for 'NAME=value' text and for shell expansions; (4) a search for standard-library calls that read the environment without naming it (getpass, tempfile, shutil.which, os.exec*, Path.home, expanduser, urllib); (5) a read of every helper, constant and table that carries a name, and of all callers. No TRON-defined name was missing. The three added names are alternative spellings that the Python standard library reads at call sites the first agent already listed. Duty C: all 98 entries were checked. Every reader site and setter site exists and names or handles the variable (342 sites). The 186 file:line references inside the prose fields and the 84 references inside the wrapper and dynamic-site descriptions were opened as well. Files with no environment access of their own: bin/compare_intermediates, bin/convert_to_safetensor.py, bin/expert_distribution.py, bin/extract_dequant, bin/fix_eagle_safetensors.py, bin/fix_mistral_tokenizer_regex.py, bin/get_model, bin/ingest_plugin_bundle.py, bin/install-nix-hooks.py, bin/load_fpga, bin/loader.py, bin/ninjatracing, bin/run_transformers, bin/safetensors_info.py, bin/split_prompt_file.py, bin/test_pio, bin/tokenize_py, bin/tps-stats, bin/tps-summary, bin/slice_bench_data.py, bin/slice_bench_manifest.py, bin/dice_lsf.py (it only parses and builds SYSTEM_CONFIG text). bin/test_ingest_plugin_bundle.py is no longer in this list: it reads TMPDIR, TEMP and TMP through tempfile. bin/loader.py runs quartus_pgm, setpci and lspci through os.system and subprocess, which search PATH. Comments and help texts that name a variable which no code reads: bin/ninjatracing:22 ($BUILDDIR, usage text only), bin/run_transformers:4 ($HOME, usage text only), bin/dice:4244 and two test docstrings ($INVOCATION_ID, named to say that it is not used). The scripts name none of them, so none is listed. bin/get_model passes its --token option to the download call; what the library does without that option was not determined. Not listed on purpose: the variables that the Python interpreter itself reads at startup (PYTHON* names, locale names), and TZ, which the C library reads for the time.strftime calls in bin/dice, bin/slice and the LSF tools.
